families.rationale: Names with the lowest share of short-sale volume outperform the heavily shorted (Boehmer, Jones and Zhang, 2008; Diether, Lee and Werner, 2009): the long leg of the daily short-flow spread.
The same light-shorting leg measured over one week of flow (the five-day aggregation of Boehmer, Jones and Zhang, 2008).
Shorting below its own recent norm: informed sellers stepping back.
The same retreat of shorting below its own norm, smoothed over one week.
Short volume below its recent mean, independent of the day's total volume.

Shorts are contrarian and step in after price rises (Diether, Lee and Werner, 2009); a rise they do not oppose continues. The score divides by the 0/1 condition, so a name without a positive week has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among rising names only.

The pre-registered opposite sign: abnormal shorting into a falling week reverses (a crowded-short bounce). The score divides by the 0/1 condition, so a name without a negative week has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among falling names only.
A low off-exchange (retail and internalised) share: names outside the retail-attention tape (Boehmer, Jones, Zhang and Zhang, 2021: retail herding precedes short-horizon reversals).

rationale: A predeclared fixed set of eight short-sale formulas, one hypothesis each, scored once without search on daily bars read at D-1 together with the four dimensionless short_fields_v1 columns (short_ratio, short_ratio_z, short_volume_rel, offex_share), so search-power check B does not apply; checks A and C still bind. The source is FINRA's Daily Short Sale Volume Files (Consolidated NMS), which cover off-exchange (TRF and ADF) volume only: the file's TotalVolume is not consolidated volume, and offex_share is an off-exchange share measure, not a short-interest figure. Each file is published the same day by 18:00 ET, so a field holding state at T is first read by decision session T+1 at 10:35 ET with at least 16 hours of slack. Trailing statistics exclude T (the baseline is the last 20 finite prior values within 40 sessions), a missing row is NaN and never carried forward, and a thin day (under 10,000 shares) has no ratio. A name change that moves a ticker onto or off a cohort symbol is an identity break: that symbol's fields are NaN before its latest break and earlier file rows are discarded. The inputs are the digest-pinned acquisition of the FINRA files (files as served at acquisition time) and the corporate-actions acquisition. The two windowed formulas divide by their 0/1 condition, so an out-of-window name has no score (NaN, ineligible) and each session's decile is taken among in-window names only. The population is cohort v2 at 5 bp with the static-percentile universe. The cohort, label cube, windows, selection, gates, bootstrap, power and null-check parameters are the matching events protocol's, so the cached cube is reused and the lane-wide confirmation window remains unused until a finalist freezes; the campaign runs only on operator approval. The fields start on 2018-08-01, so the first of the four equal-session discovery blocks (2016-08-01 to about 2017-12-05) carries no short-volume score and the second (to about 2019-04-17) is scored only from August 2018: the discovery gate's 3 of 4 positive blocks is effectively 3 of 3, and check A, which plants its edge over the full window, slightly overstates this lane's power for small edges.
title: Short-volume pooled campaign v1: cohort v2, daily bars read at D-1 plus the four short_fields_v1 FINRA short-sale fields, predeclared fixed set of eight formulas (checks A and C), one-shot lane-wide confirmation
